city.description: City the customer is registered in (may differ from orders.shipping_city).

products.description: Product catalog with current list price and cost.

is_active.description: Whether the product is currently sold.

orders.description: One row per order (order header). Every order has exactly one payment row.

status.description: Fulfilment status of the order. Cancelled orders are excluded from all business metrics (order counts, revenue, customers who ordered, ...) unless the user explicitly asks to include them.

order_items.description: Order lines: one row per product in an order.

unit_price.description: Unit price recorded on the order line.

unit_cost.description: Unit cost recorded on the order line.

discount_rate.description: Line discount as a fraction between 0 and 1 (0.1 = 10%).

payments.description: One payment row per order (order_id is unique).

paid_at.description: Payment date, ISO text. NULL when status is pending or failed.

amount.description: Payment amount for the whole order.

terms.name: revenue
terms.definition: Collected revenue: sum of payments.amount where payments.status = 'paid' and the order is not cancelled (orders.status <> 'cancelled'). Pending, failed and refunded payments are excluded. Some cancelled orders still show a 'paid' payment; they are excluded too. payments.amount equals the discounted line total of the order. 'Top customers by sales' means ranking by this revenue.
terms.sql: SELECT SUM(p.amount) FROM payments p JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.order_id WHERE p.status = 'paid' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

terms.name: order count
terms.definition: Number of orders that are not cancelled (orders.status <> 'cancelled'), regardless of payment status.
terms.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'

terms.name: profit
terms.definition: Gross profit on the same orders as revenue (paid payment, not cancelled): sum over order_items of quantity * (unit_price * (1 - discount_rate) - unit_cost). The discount reduces the price, not the cost.
terms.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_rate) - oi.unit_cost)) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id WHERE p.status = 'paid' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

terms.name: profit margin
terms.definition: Profit divided by discounted line revenue on the same orders (paid, not cancelled). A fraction; multiply by 100 for a percentage.
terms.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_rate) - oi.unit_cost)) * 1.0 / SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_rate)) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id WHERE p.status = 'paid' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

terms.name: average order value
terms.definition: Revenue divided by the number of orders counted in revenue (paid payment, not cancelled).
terms.sql: SELECT SUM(p.amount) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) FROM payments p JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.order_id WHERE p.status = 'paid' AND o.status <> 'cancelled'

terms.name: new customer
terms.definition: A customer whose first non-cancelled order (MIN(orders.ordered_at) with orders.status <> 'cancelled') falls in the period. For signups use 'new signup' instead. The example SQL uses Q3 2026; replace the dates.
terms.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, MIN(o.ordered_at) AS first_order FROM orders o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id) f WHERE f.first_order BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'

terms.name: new signup
terms.definition: A customer whose signup date (customers.joined_at) falls in the period, whether or not they ordered. The example SQL uses Q3 2026; replace the dates.
terms.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c WHERE c.joined_at BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'

terms.name: active customer
terms.definition: A customer with at least one non-cancelled order in the 90 days up to the latest order date in the data (not today's date, because the dataset is static).
terms.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) FROM orders o WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.ordered_at >= date((SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders), '-90 day')
